name: SysBench
intro: SysBench用于系统评测大语言模型遵循系统消息的能力，包含500个五轮会话和2500轮用户交互，覆盖6类可验证约束、对齐与不对齐指令，以及并行与依赖多轮关系。
build_method: 真实日志收集, 启发式与聚类清洗, GPT-4o辅助, 人工重写与检查表标注
metric: Constraint Satisfaction Rate, Instruction Satisfaction Rate, Session Stability Rate
build_method_en: Real-log collection, heuristic and clustering cleanup, GPT-4o assistance, human rewriting and checklist annotation
intro_en: SysBench systematically evaluates whether LLMs follow system messages. It contains 500 five-turn sessions and 2,500 user turns spanning six verifiable constraint types, aligned and misaligned instructions, and parallel and dependent multi-turn relations.
metric_en: Constraint Satisfaction Rate, Instruction Satisfaction Rate, Session Stability Rate

drawio_review_note: Aligned with SysBench arXiv:2408.10943 Section 3 and Appendix A; official PKU-Baichuan-MLSystemLab/SysBench repository. SysBench starts from thousands of system messages in online logs and defines six atomic, verifiable constraint types: action, content, background, role, format, and style. Heuristic rules and clustering remove duplicates and noise. Twenty-one trained annotators select and refine 500 system messages for explicit tasks and diverse constraints. GPT-4o assists conversation generation; annotators retain and rewrite five user rounds per system message under expert guidelines. The 500 sessions contain 2,500 turns: 144 parallel and 356 dependent sessions, with 1,951 aligned and 549 misaligned instructions and 2.38 constraints per instruction on average. Annotators write a checklist for every instruction, and multiple experts perform independent multi-round review. During evaluation, the target model receives the system message, conversation history, and current user instruction. An advanced-LLM verifier receives the same context plus the checklist and judges every relevant constraint as binary satisfied or not. Constraint Satisfaction Rate averages atomic checks, Instruction Satisfaction Rate requires all constraints in a response, and Session Stability Rate measures the consecutive fully satisfied prefix from the start of each dialogue.
